#4471 · date parsing causes and outcomes

owner support deskknownreviewed 2026-10-28

Why #4471 needed two tickets

The desk merged reports by subject, but matching subjects did not mean every report had the same cause. The export contains overlapping rows, so the cause table counts each report ID once and uses the tenant's locale, booking form and report channel. Intake tags are guesses.

Cause 1: the shared parser flips day-first dates

The shared parser reads month first. For day-first tenants, dates can therefore land on the wrong day. The export's one-day-move reports still belong to this cause under the tenant rules. Track this cause in issue #1.

Cause 2: booking-v3 gives day-first tenants a conflicting hint

The v3 form displays MM/DD/YYYY for tenants whose locale writes day first. A customer can follow that hint while the tenant-side parser reads the date in the opposite order. Track it separately in issue #2.

Counts de-duplicate by report ID and group by tenant configuration and channel. The five reports noted as one-day moves remain in the parser group; they do not establish a third cause.

Engineering outcome

The desk closed #4471 on 5 October. Engineering fixed the shared parser with fix(dates): parse dd/mm for eu locales. The v3-form issue will not be fixed because booking-v3 was retired.
